connection_condition: an atom carries the molecule_id of its owning molecule
description: A molecule is composed of its atoms; every atom belongs to exactly one molecule and has no meaning without it.

connection_condition: a bond carries the molecule_id of its owning molecule
description: A molecule is composed of its bonds; every bond belongs to exactly one molecule.
Carcinogenic molecules are a subset of molecules, defined by one value of the carcinogenicity label.
Non-carcinogenic molecules are a subset of molecules, defined by the other value of the carcinogenicity label.
A single bond is a specific kind of bond; its value domain is the single-bond code, a subset of the bond type value domain.
A double bond is a specific kind of bond; its value domain is the double-bond code, a subset of the bond type value domain.
A triple bond is a specific kind of bond; its value domain is the triple-bond code, a subset of the bond type value domain.

connection_condition: molecule.label holds the carcinogenicity code of the molecule identified by molecule.molecule_id
description: The carcinogenicity label is the molecule-level attribute that determines whether a molecule counts as carcinogenic.

connection_condition: atom.element holds the element symbol of the atom identified by atom.atom_id
description: An atom carries exactly one chemical element, which determines how it contributes to a molecule's composition.

connection_condition: bond.bond_type holds the bond order code of the bond identified by bond.bond_id
description: The bond type is the attribute that distinguishes single, double, and triple bonds.

connection_condition: the connectivity relation associates a bond_id with exactly two endpoint atom references
description: Each bond joins exactly two atoms of its molecule; this is the structural relationship that makes bond counts and atom counts comparable.

connection_condition: each connectivity row pairs a bond reference with one of the two atom references that bond joins
description: The atom adjacency relation is derived by pairing each bond with the two atoms it joins.

connection_condition: molecule.molecule_id, atom.molecule_id, and bond.molecule_id share the same value domain
description: The molecule identifier appears both as the molecule table key and as the reference carried by atoms and bonds, so molecule-level attributes can be attached to child records through it.

connection_condition: the endpoint atom references in the connectivity relation hold the same atom identifiers as atom.atom_id
description: Atom references used to describe which atoms a bond joins denote the same atoms as the atom table, so element information reached through either representation is the same.

connection_condition: the bond reference in the connectivity relation holds the same bond identifiers as bond.bond_id
description: The bond reference carried by adjacency rows denotes the same bond records as the bond table, so bond-level attributes such as bond type apply to it.
The carcinogenic share is derived from the molecule-level carcinogenicity labels as the count of carcinogenic-labelled molecules over the count of all molecules in scope.
The element atom count is derived by counting distinct atoms per element symbol, optionally restricted by the carcinogenicity class of their molecules.
The bond type frequency is derived by counting bonds per bond type code within the stated molecule scope.
The within-molecule element ratio is derived from the count of atoms of that element and the total atom count of the same molecule.
The average number of bonds per atom is derived from the atom adjacency relation as the number of bond incidences divided by the number of distinct atoms in the set.
